candidate.title: Project Cut
candidate.problemStatement: A successor agent cannot determine which available source, Atlas, Episode, policy, omission, risk, and predecessor roots were officially admitted together merely by reading open work state or the component authorities independently.
candidate.scope: Accepted as a software-project settlement Primitive under KFD-12; it is not a fourth fact engine, universal cross-domain object, completion proof, historical novelty claim, or activation of KFD-12.

observationPerspective.bearer: human or agent maintaining software work, responsibility, context, and decisions
observationPerspective.proximity: inside the Initiative and Assignment lifecycle
consequences: bears stale work state, missing responsibility, and incomplete review

genesis.observation: Maintaining Initiative and Assignment state appeared sufficient from the coordinator view. Moving to the successor agent's action position exposed the repeated need for one exact answer to what the project officially became and which settled boundary may be continued without re-adjudicating every prior work object.
genesis.candidateObject: A Project Cut is an independently addressable software-project macro commitment that binds selected predecessor, source, Atlas, Episode, policy, omission, conflict, unknown, and residual-risk roots without absorbing their authorities.
genesis.claimBoundary: The cut accepts the higher-layer settlement responsibility within software projects. It does not claim that Project Cut is another fact engine, that valid settlement proves work quality or release fitness, or that every domain needs the same object.

methodEvidence.observer: human maintainer testimony about agent-origin genesis
Kungfu Project Cut architecture and review
Kungfu agent-first settlement implementation and review

transformedPerspective.bearer: an agent receiving a project after prior work and settlement
transformedPerspective.role: successor verifier and bounded continuation actor
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside reconstruction, trust, retry, and next-action consequences
consequences: bears repeated investigation, stale continuation, wrong source selection, and unverified authority binding

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from maintaining the work graph to the downstream agent that must verify one bounded project state before safely continuing.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: A successor needs one deterministic, independently checkable macro commitment selecting which exact component roots were officially admitted together, without replaying the entire management context.
genesis.methodNotes: The human maintainer reports agent-origin candidate generation. Git proves the later submitted architecture, implementation, tests, and review but not the private conversational authorship claim.

contactSides: the participants and authorities that produced source, Atlas, Episode, policy, and work decisions
the successor agent, reviewer, release process, or clean clone that must continue from the accepted project state
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: The binding is reconstructed from Git ancestry, latest files, task state, context, release notes, caches, and participant memory.

pressureChanges.description: Successor agents and independent reviewers do not share the producer's transient context.
Source, Atlas, Episode, policy, and review systems retain different roots and authority semantics.
Choosing the wrong combination changes what code, knowledge, causal history, omissions, and risks the successor treats as official.
Re-adjudicating prior work before every continuation makes handoff and recovery expensive.

observedFailures: A Git commit is mistaken for causal or epistemic settlement.
A valid Atlas or Episode root is treated as complete project identity.
A successor must inspect many management records to infer the accepted component set.
Hooks, caches, or prior conversations become hidden authority for continuation.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: Project Cut may publish one deterministic cross-authority settlement binding that successors can verify without converting it into a new component authority.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: A release manifest, provenance envelope, snapshot, or commit attestation may implement equivalent Project Cut semantics if it binds the same authorities, omissions, risks, and predecessor relation.

pressure: Successor agents need one exact continuation boundary rather than the complete Initiative and Assignment context.
Git, Atlas, and Episode roots remain independently authoritative and cannot replace one another.
Settlement must survive hooks, caches, GUI state, Git rewrites, clean clones, concurrent work, and missing private context.
grounding.evidenceBoundary: Public Kungfu architecture, deterministic root implementation, agent-first settlement, stage-0 recovery, Git-history bindings, clean-clone continuation, independent review, three-agent dogfood, and concurrent composition support one software-project profile. The private agent-origin conversation is not independently retained.
knownGaps: Private conversational authorship cannot be reconstructed from Git
Release fitness and work correctness remain external assessments

alternatives.name: Maintain Initiative and Assignment state only
alternatives.reason: Work state does not by itself select and publish which independent authority roots form the official successor project boundary.

alternatives.name: Git commit, tag, or release
alternatives.reason: Git publishes bytes and ancestry but does not own causal, perspective, omission, policy, risk, or completion semantics.

alternatives.name: Fact Cut, Atlas, Episode, or latest database state
alternatives.reason: Each remains authoritative for its own domain and cannot select the cross-authority settlement without adding an equivalent binding.

alternatives.name: Release manifest, provenance envelope, or snapshot
alternatives.reason: These may implement equivalent Project Cut semantics when they preserve exact roots, predecessor, omissions, risk, independent verification, and no authority absorption.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: The deletion witness changes which exact state a successor may treat as officially settled while every component remains available.

contractModel.identity: A deterministic project_cut_root over one canonical settlement preimage, independent from its outer Git publication coordinate.
contractModel.boundary: Predecessor Project Cut roots, accepted source projection, successor Atlas, admitted Episode delta, interpretation policy and protocol roots, omissions, conflicts, unknowns, residual risk, receipt, and outer publication relation.
contractModel.authority: Project Cut selects and binds exact roots but cannot reinterpret source, Atlas, Episode, policy, claim, assessment, decision, completion, or release authority.
contractModel.lifecycle: prepared -> sealed-unpublished -> published and reconciled -> succeeded by another cut, rejected, or retained as historical lineage; published cuts remain immutable

minimumClosure.notes: The canonical root and settlement contracts retain exact predecessor, source, Atlas, Episode, policy, omission, risk, receipt, and publication boundaries without self-reference.

deletion.notes: Without Project Cut, a successor must reselect and re-adjudicate which available component roots form the official project state.

fuse.notes: Fusing Project Cut with Git, Atlas, Episode, Fact, or completion authority creates circular identity or silent reinterpretation; equivalent settlement manifests remain allowed.

falsifiers: Successors can derive the accepted component set and omissions from existing authorities with lower cost and no hidden policy.
Independent implementations cannot reproduce the same root or continuation decision.
Project Cut becomes a second fact, source, Atlas, Episode, completion, or release authority.
The binding cannot survive clean-clone, Git-history, missing-cache, and concurrent-publication conditions.
A simpler retained manifest preserves all required decisions with less lifecycle and verification burden.

dogfood.notes: Retained first-party evidence covers agent-first settlement, public Episode integration, three-agent independent review and continuation, clean-clone rebuild, Git history, and concurrent composition.

decision.reason: Within the KFD-12 software-project profile, Project Cut preserves the independently necessary selection and settlement of exact authority roots, has a closed non-self-referential contract, and survives retained agent-first, recovery, review, and composition pressure.
residualRisks: The object may map to an existing release manifest or provenance envelope in other systems.
The qualification evidence remains first-party to Kungfu.
A convenient Project Cut could be misread as proof of correctness, completion, or release fitness.
The agent-origin genesis claim relies on maintainer testimony rather than retained transcript evidence.
Cross-domain use and historical novelty are unqualified.
